source_row.rationale: Anaphylaxis can recur after apparent initial resolution as a biphasic reaction, so continued observation may be appropriate based on severity, treatment needs, and risk factors. Option A is correct. Biphasic reactions are not inevitable or predictably timed, do not require a new exposure, and are not caused by residual epinephrine.
source_row.source_detail: Post-anaphylaxis monitoring: symptoms can resolve and later return as a biphasic reaction; emergency evaluation/monitoring is appropriate after treatment and observation is individualized according to the reaction and clinical course. Current AAAAI anaphylaxis guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation: acute/complex alterations, emergency response and pathophysiologic adaptation. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: After treatment for anaphylaxis, a client's symptoms have completely resolved. Why may continued observation still be appropriate?
